# Refusals

The specific reasons a request, a revision, a solve or a project is refused, named inside an API error, a validation check or a failed run. How to read an explanation, and how to ask for one (`openflowsheet explain <code>`, the `explain` operation), is on [Messages](index.md).

<a id="ambient_pressure_invalid"></a>

## `ambient_pressure_invalid`: An ambient pressure that cannot be declared

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The ambient pressure was not declared: its &lt;part&gt; is not accepted (&lt;value&gt; &lt;unit&gt;).
- **Why:** The ambient pressure is the absolute pressure gauge readings are measured from, so it must be a finite pressure above zero, written in an absolute unit: Pa, kPa, MPa, bar, atm or psi. A gauge unit (barg, psig) cannot declare it, and other spellings (bara, mmHg) are not accepted. Nothing is assumed in its place, and the project file is left as it was.
- **Do:** Declare it again with a finite value above zero in one of Pa, kPa, MPa, bar, atm or psi, for example --pressure 1.01325 --unit bar.
- **Parameters:** `part` (text), `value` (text, optional), `unit` (text, optional)
- **See also:** [`ambient_pressure_undeclared`](#ambient_pressure_undeclared)

Example:

```text
The ambient pressure was not declared: the value -1.0 is not a finite pressure above zero in bar.
  Why:     The ambient pressure is the absolute pressure gauge readings are measured from, so it must be a finite pressure above zero, written in an absolute unit: Pa, kPa, MPa, bar, atm or psi. A gauge unit (barg, psig) cannot declare it, and other spellings (bara, mmHg) are not accepted. Nothing is assumed in its place, and the project file is left as it was.
  Do:      Declare it again with a finite value above zero in one of Pa, kPa, MPa, bar, atm or psi, for example --pressure 1.01325 --unit bar.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    ambient_pressure_invalid (openflowsheet explain ambient_pressure_invalid)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#ambient_pressure_invalid
```

Example:

```text
The ambient pressure was not declared: the unit barg is not an absolute pressure unit it can be written in.
  Why:     The ambient pressure is the absolute pressure gauge readings are measured from, so it must be a finite pressure above zero, written in an absolute unit: Pa, kPa, MPa, bar, atm or psi. A gauge unit (barg, psig) cannot declare it, and other spellings (bara, mmHg) are not accepted. Nothing is assumed in its place, and the project file is left as it was.
  Do:      Declare it again with a finite value above zero in one of Pa, kPa, MPa, bar, atm or psi, for example --pressure 1.01325 --unit bar.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    ambient_pressure_invalid (openflowsheet explain ambient_pressure_invalid)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#ambient_pressure_invalid
```

<a id="ambient_pressure_undeclared"></a>

## `ambient_pressure_undeclared`: A gauge display unit in a project without an ambient pressure

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** Pressures cannot be shown as gauge pressures in &lt;unit&gt;: the project has no declared ambient pressure.
- **Where:** the request member display_units
- **Why:** A gauge pressure is the absolute pressure minus the ambient pressure of the site. OpenFlowsheet never assumes an ambient pressure (not even one standard atmosphere): it uses the one the project declares, and this project declares none.
- **Do:** Ask the project's operator to declare it with openflowsheet project ambient --project DIR --pressure VALUE --unit UNIT, or show pressures in an absolute unit such as bar.
- **Parameters:** `kind` (text), `unit` (text, optional)
- **See also:** [`ambient_pressure_invalid`](#ambient_pressure_invalid), [`display_units_invalid`](#display_units_invalid)

Example:

```text
Pressures cannot be shown as gauge pressures in barg: the project has no declared ambient pressure.
  Why:     A gauge pressure is the absolute pressure minus the ambient pressure of the site. OpenFlowsheet never assumes an ambient pressure (not even one standard atmosphere): it uses the one the project declares, and this project declares none.
  Do:      Ask the project's operator to declare it with openflowsheet project ambient --project DIR --pressure VALUE --unit UNIT, or show pressures in an absolute unit such as bar.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    ambient_pressure_undeclared (openflowsheet explain ambient_pressure_undeclared)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#ambient_pressure_undeclared
```

<a id="capability_missing"></a>

## `capability_missing`: The unit model cannot be used with this property method

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** Unit model &lt;unit&gt; is not admitted with property method &lt;method&gt;: nothing provides &lt;capability&gt;.
- **Why:** A unit model states the capabilities it needs from the property method and from the stream definition, and a property method states those it needs from the stream definition. A pair is admitted only when every stated need is met. A capability written as several tokens separated by a vertical bar is met by any one of them.
- **Do:** Choose a property method that provides &lt;capability&gt;, or a unit model that does not need it. The list_capabilities operation lists what each registered model and method requires and provides; check_admission tests a pair.
- **Parameters:** `unit` (text), `method` (text), `capability` (text)
- **Not supported:** missing capability: a property method or stream definition that provides the capability the error names
- **See also:** [`model_unsupported`](#model_unsupported), [`capability_unresolved`](notices.md#capability_unresolved)

Example:

```text
Unit model thermal.heater is not admitted with property method pr-lib-v1: nothing provides conn:nTP-v1.
  Why:     A unit model states the capabilities it needs from the property method and from the stream definition, and a property method states those it needs from the stream definition. A pair is admitted only when every stated need is met. A capability written as several tokens separated by a vertical bar is met by any one of them.
  Do:      Choose a property method that provides conn:nTP-v1, or a unit model that does not need it. The list_capabilities operation lists what each registered model and method requires and provides; check_admission tests a pair.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    capability_missing (openflowsheet explain capability_missing)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#capability_missing
```

<a id="capability_unknown"></a>

## `capability_unknown`: An extension names a capability the registry does not know

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The capability &lt;token&gt; is not known, so the extension that declares it is not loaded.
- **Why:** A capability is written space:name, with an optional level. Its space must be one of the registry's spaces, and in a space whose names are a fixed list (vocab, flash, convention, legacy) the name must be on that list. One unknown capability keeps the whole extension package out of the registry; other packages are unaffected.
- **Do:** Correct the capability in the extension's descriptor, or remove it, and reinstall the extension.
- **Parameters:** `token` (text)
- **See also:** [`reserved_capability`](#reserved_capability)

Example:

```text
The capability flash:PH is not known, so the extension that declares it is not loaded.
  Why:     A capability is written space:name, with an optional level. Its space must be one of the registry's spaces, and in a space whose names are a fixed list (vocab, flash, convention, legacy) the name must be on that list. One unknown capability keeps the whole extension package out of the registry; other packages are unaffected.
  Do:      Correct the capability in the extension's descriptor, or remove it, and reinstall the extension.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    capability_unknown (openflowsheet explain capability_unknown)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#capability_unknown
```

<a id="dependency_missing"></a>

## `dependency_missing`: An extension's optional dependencies are not installed

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** The extension &lt;id&gt; needs the optional dependencies of the extra &lt;extra&gt;, which are not installed.
- **Why:** An extension's descriptor names the install extra that brings its optional dependencies. Importing its implementation failed, so those dependencies are missing from this Python environment.
- **Do:** Install the extra, for example pip install with the package name followed by &lt;extra&gt;, then retry.
- **Parameters:** `id` (text), `extra` (text)
- **Not supported:** missing capability: the optional dependencies of this extension
- **See also:** [`platform_unsupported`](#platform_unsupported)

Example:

```text
The extension lca needs the optional dependencies of the extra lca, which are not installed.
  Why:     An extension's descriptor names the install extra that brings its optional dependencies. Importing its implementation failed, so those dependencies are missing from this Python environment.
  Do:      Install the extra, for example pip install with the package name followed by lca, then retry.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    dependency_missing (openflowsheet explain dependency_missing)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#dependency_missing
```

<a id="directory_not_empty"></a>

## `directory_not_empty`: The directory holds files that are not a project

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** Directory &lt;directory&gt; is not empty and does not hold a project; a project needs a new or empty directory.
- **Why:** OpenFlowsheet will not mix a project with other files, and exist_ok=True opens only an existing project.
- **Do:** Choose a new directory name, or empty this directory first.
- **Parameters:** `directory` (directory)

Example:

```text
Directory 'notes' is not empty and does not hold a project; a project needs a new or empty directory.
  Why:     OpenFlowsheet will not mix a project with other files, and exist_ok=True opens only an existing project.
  Do:      Choose a new directory name, or empty this directory first.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    directory_not_empty (openflowsheet explain directory_not_empty)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#directory_not_empty
```

<a id="display_unit_unsupported"></a>

## `display_unit_unsupported`: A display unit this version does not offer for the kind

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** Values of kind &lt;kind&gt; cannot be shown in &lt;unit&gt;: the unit is not one this version offers for that kind.
- **Where:** the request member display_units
- **Why:** Each quantity kind is shown in its SI unit or in one of a fixed list of units, each spelled exactly as in the input table: degC, not °C or celsius; bar or barg, not bara. Some kinds, such as molar heat capacity, have no display units besides SI in this version.
- **Do:** Use one of the units the units guide lists for &lt;kind&gt;, spelled exactly, or the kind's SI unit to show it unconverted.
- **Parameters:** `kind` (text), `unit` (text, optional)
- **Not supported:** 
- **See also:** [`display_units_invalid`](#display_units_invalid)

Example:

```text
Values of kind temperature cannot be shown in celsius: the unit is not one this version offers for that kind.
  Why:     Each quantity kind is shown in its SI unit or in one of a fixed list of units, each spelled exactly as in the input table: degC, not °C or celsius; bar or barg, not bara. Some kinds, such as molar heat capacity, have no display units besides SI in this version.
  Do:      Use one of the units the units guide lists for temperature, spelled exactly, or the kind's SI unit to show it unconverted.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    display_unit_unsupported (openflowsheet explain display_unit_unsupported)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#display_unit_unsupported
```

Example:

```text
Values of kind molar_heat_capacity cannot be shown in kJ/(mol K): the unit is not one this version offers for that kind.
  Why:     Each quantity kind is shown in its SI unit or in one of a fixed list of units, each spelled exactly as in the input table: degC, not °C or celsius; bar or barg, not bara. Some kinds, such as molar heat capacity, have no display units besides SI in this version.
  Do:      Use one of the units the units guide lists for molar_heat_capacity, spelled exactly, or the kind's SI unit to show it unconverted.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    display_unit_unsupported (openflowsheet explain display_unit_unsupported)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#display_unit_unsupported
```

<a id="display_units_invalid"></a>

## `display_units_invalid`: A display units preference that cannot be read

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The display units preference was not read: item &lt;index&gt; (&lt;item&gt;) is not a preset or a kind=unit pair it accepts.
- **Where:** the request member display_units
- **Why:** display_units is a comma-separated list read left to right. The first item may be a preset (si or eng); every other item is kind=unit, where kind is a quantity kind such as temperature or molar_flow, named at most once. An unknown kind, a missing '=' or unit, a preset after the first item, or a kind named twice is refused, and nothing is converted.
- **Do:** Write display_units as an optional preset followed by kind=unit items, for example eng,temperature=degF; the units guide lists the kinds and their units.
- **Parameters:** `index` (number), `item` (text, optional)
- **See also:** [`display_unit_unsupported`](#display_unit_unsupported), [`ambient_pressure_undeclared`](#ambient_pressure_undeclared)

Example:

```text
The display units preference was not read: item 0 (temp=degC) is not a preset or a kind=unit pair it accepts.
  Why:     display_units is a comma-separated list read left to right. The first item may be a preset (si or eng); every other item is kind=unit, where kind is a quantity kind such as temperature or molar_flow, named at most once. An unknown kind, a missing '=' or unit, a preset after the first item, or a kind named twice is refused, and nothing is converted.
  Do:      Write display_units as an optional preset followed by kind=unit items, for example eng,temperature=degF; the units guide lists the kinds and their units.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    display_units_invalid (openflowsheet explain display_units_invalid)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#display_units_invalid
```

Example:

```text
The display units preference was not read: item 1.000 (eng) is not a preset or a kind=unit pair it accepts.
  Why:     display_units is a comma-separated list read left to right. The first item may be a preset (si or eng); every other item is kind=unit, where kind is a quantity kind such as temperature or molar_flow, named at most once. An unknown kind, a missing '=' or unit, a preset after the first item, or a kind named twice is refused, and nothing is converted.
  Do:      Write display_units as an optional preset followed by kind=unit items, for example eng,temperature=degF; the units guide lists the kinds and their units.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    display_units_invalid (openflowsheet explain display_units_invalid)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#display_units_invalid
```

<a id="energy_balance_undefined"></a>

## `energy_balance_undefined`: The energy balance of this unit model is not checked

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** The energy balance of unit &lt;unit&gt; (&lt;model&gt;) is not given: the solution's certificate holds no energy check for it.
- **Where:** unit &lt;unit&gt;
- **Why:** The stream table reports a unit's energy balance only where the certificate of the solution holds an energy check for that unit. Units of this model carry none (an external or coupled unit, for example), so the unit's duty, work and stream enthalpy flows are reported, but its balance is not.
- **Do:** Use a unit model whose energy balance is checked if you need this balance; the stream values around &lt;unit&gt; are unaffected.
- **Parameters:** `unit` (unit), `model` (text)
- **Not supported:** missing capability: an energy balance check for this unit's model
- **See also:** [`stream_enthalpy_absent`](notices.md#stream_enthalpy_absent)

Example:

```text
The energy balance of unit 'X1' (external.coupled) is not given: the solution's certificate holds no energy check for it.
  Why:     The stream table reports a unit's energy balance only where the certificate of the solution holds an energy check for that unit. Units of this model carry none (an external or coupled unit, for example), so the unit's duty, work and stream enthalpy flows are reported, but its balance is not.
  Do:      Use a unit model whose energy balance is checked if you need this balance; the stream values around 'X1' are unaffected.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    energy_balance_undefined (openflowsheet explain energy_balance_undefined)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#energy_balance_undefined
```

<a id="extension_invalid"></a>

## `extension_invalid`: An extension package does not match the descriptor format

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The extension package of entry point &lt;entry_point&gt; is not valid at &lt;pointer&gt;, so it is not loaded.
- **Why:** Every extension package is checked before anything of it is registered: its document against the extension descriptor schema, its namespace against the entry point's name, each id against the namespace, each message catalogue against the message format, and each limitation code against the catalogue. The location is a JSON pointer into the package document.
- **Do:** Correct the package document at the location given and reinstall the extension.
- **Parameters:** `entry_point` (text), `pointer` (text)

Example:

```text
The extension package of entry point acme is not valid at /descriptors/0/version, so it is not loaded.
  Why:     Every extension package is checked before anything of it is registered: its document against the extension descriptor schema, its namespace against the entry point's name, each id against the namespace, each message catalogue against the message format, and each limitation code against the catalogue. The location is a JSON pointer into the package document.
  Do:      Correct the package document at the location given and reinstall the extension.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    extension_invalid (openflowsheet explain extension_invalid)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#extension_invalid
```

<a id="extension_load_failed"></a>

## `extension_load_failed`: An extension's entry point could not be loaded

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The entry point &lt;entry_point&gt; could not be loaded, or raised an error, so its extension is not loaded.
- **Why:** The registry imports each extension's entry point and calls it for its package document. The import failed or the call raised an exception; the exception's class is written to the log, not to this message.
- **Do:** Import the entry point's module in the same Python environment to see the error, correct the extension and reinstall it.
- **Parameters:** `entry_point` (text)

Example:

```text
The entry point acme could not be loaded, or raised an error, so its extension is not loaded.
  Why:     The registry imports each extension's entry point and calls it for its package document. The import failed or the call raised an exception; the exception's class is written to the log, not to this message.
  Do:      Import the entry point's module in the same Python environment to see the error, correct the extension and reinstall it.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    extension_load_failed (openflowsheet explain extension_load_failed)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#extension_load_failed
```

<a id="factory_unavailable"></a>

## `factory_unavailable`: A registered extension cannot be constructed

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** The &lt;kind&gt; &lt;id&gt; is registered and listed, but this version cannot construct it.
- **Why:** Some registered extensions are listed so that their capabilities can be inspected, but they have no constructor this version may use: their descriptor names none, or the property method is registered without being selectable for a flowsheet.
- **Do:** Choose another &lt;kind&gt;; the list_capabilities operation lists the registered ones.
- **Parameters:** `kind` (text), `id` (text)
- **Not supported:** missing capability: a constructor for this registered extension
- **See also:** [`platform_unsupported`](#platform_unsupported), [`dependency_missing`](#dependency_missing)

Example:

```text
The property_method pr-lib-v1 is registered and listed, but this version cannot construct it.
  Why:     Some registered extensions are listed so that their capabilities can be inspected, but they have no constructor this version may use: their descriptor names none, or the property method is registered without being selectable for a flowsheet.
  Do:      Choose another property_method; the list_capabilities operation lists the registered ones.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    factory_unavailable (openflowsheet explain factory_unavailable)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#factory_unavailable
```

<a id="flash_failed"></a>

## `flash_failed`: The phase split of a stream could not be computed

**Kind:** Numerical failure: the solver did not find the solution; your flowsheet may be correct.

- **Summary:** The phase split of stream &lt;stream&gt; at its temperature and pressure could not be computed (status &lt;status&gt;).
- **Where:** stream &lt;stream&gt;
- **Why:** For a stream whose phases are neither declared nor carried by the solution, the stream table finds them with an equilibrium flash at the stored temperature and pressure. That flash did not succeed, so the phases of &lt;stream&gt; and the values per phase are not given; its flows, temperature and pressure are.
- **Do:** Check that the temperature and pressure of &lt;stream&gt; lie in the range the property basis covers. A phase declared for the stream lets the table evaluate it without a flash.
- **Parameters:** `stream` (stream), `status` (text, optional)
- **See also:** [`stream_enthalpy_absent`](notices.md#stream_enthalpy_absent)

Example:

```text
The phase split of stream 'S3' at its temperature and pressure could not be computed (status failed).
  Why:     For a stream whose phases are neither declared nor carried by the solution, the stream table finds them with an equilibrium flash at the stored temperature and pressure. That flash did not succeed, so the phases of 'S3' and the values per phase are not given; its flows, temperature and pressure are.
  Do:      Check that the temperature and pressure of 'S3' lie in the range the property basis covers. A phase declared for the stream lets the table evaluate it without a flash.
  Kind:    Numerical failure: the solver did not find the solution; your flowsheet may be correct.
  Code:    flash_failed (openflowsheet explain flash_failed)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#flash_failed
```

<a id="initializer_failed"></a>

## `initializer_failed`: The first pass over the flowsheet stopped at a unit

**Kind:** Numerical failure: the solver did not find the solution; your flowsheet may be correct.

- **Summary:** The first pass over the flowsheet could not compute every unit (it stopped at &lt;unit&gt;).
- **Why:** Before iterating, OpenFlowsheet computes every unit once, in flow order; this pass stopped.
- **Do:** Read the cause; if none is given, supply an initial guess for the recycle streams.
- **Parameters:** `unit` (element)

Example:

```text
The first pass over the flowsheet could not compute every unit (it stopped at 'T').
  Why:     Before iterating, OpenFlowsheet computes every unit once, in flow order; this pass stopped.
  Do:      Read the cause; if none is given, supply an initial guess for the recycle streams.
  Kind:    Numerical failure: the solver did not find the solution; your flowsheet may be correct.
  Code:    initializer_failed (openflowsheet explain initializer_failed)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#initializer_failed
```

<a id="isentropic_state_single_phase"></a>

## `isentropic_state_single_phase`: A machine whose ideal outlet is single-phase, unlike its declared outlet

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** The machine &lt;unit&gt; needs a case this version does not support: its ideal (isentropic) outlet state is single-phase, not the phase declared for its outlet.
- **Why:** This version computes a machine's ideal outlet in the phase declared for the real outlet. Here the outlet is declared wet ("vapor_liquid") but the ideal outlet lies outside the two-phase region, or, where the fluid has no two-phase region at the outlet pressure, the ideal outlet is of another phase than the one declared. This is a limitation of the software, not an error in your flowsheet.
- **Do:** Declare the outlet with the phase its ideal state has (for example vapour when the ideal state is superheated) if the real outlet has that phase too; otherwise change the operating conditions until the ideal and the real outlet are in the same phase.
- **Parameters:** `unit` (unit, optional)
- **Not supported:** missing capability: an ideal (isentropic) outlet of another phase than the declared outlet
- **See also:** [`isentropic_state_two_phase`](#isentropic_state_two_phase), [`phase_regime_mismatch`](#phase_regime_mismatch)

Example:

```text
The solve stopped before its first iteration: unit 'T' could not compute its outlets from the starting values.
  Cause:   The machine 'T' needs a case this version does not support: its ideal (isentropic) outlet state is single-phase, not the phase declared for its outlet.
  Why:     This version computes a machine's ideal outlet in the phase declared for the real outlet. Here the outlet is declared wet ("vapor_liquid") but the ideal outlet lies outside the two-phase region, or, where the fluid has no two-phase region at the outlet pressure, the ideal outlet is of another phase than the one declared. This is a limitation of the software, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Do:      Declare the outlet with the phase its ideal state has (for example vapour when the ideal state is superheated) if the real outlet has that phase too; otherwise change the operating conditions until the ideal and the real outlet are in the same phase.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    isentropic_state_single_phase, in INITIALIZATION_FAILED → initializer_failed (openflowsheet explain isentropic_state_single_phase)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#isentropic_state_single_phase
```

Example:

```text
The machine needs a case this version does not support: its ideal (isentropic) outlet state is single-phase, not the phase declared for its outlet.
  Why:     This version computes a machine's ideal outlet in the phase declared for the real outlet. Here the outlet is declared wet ("vapor_liquid") but the ideal outlet lies outside the two-phase region, or, where the fluid has no two-phase region at the outlet pressure, the ideal outlet is of another phase than the one declared. This is a limitation of the software, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Do:      Declare the outlet with the phase its ideal state has (for example vapour when the ideal state is superheated) if the real outlet has that phase too; otherwise change the operating conditions until the ideal and the real outlet are in the same phase.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    isentropic_state_single_phase (openflowsheet explain isentropic_state_single_phase)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#isentropic_state_single_phase
```

<a id="isentropic_state_two_phase"></a>

## `isentropic_state_two_phase`: A turbine whose ideal outlet would be wet while its outlet is declared vapour

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** Unit &lt;unit&gt; needs a case this version does not support: its outlet &lt;outlet&gt; is declared vapour, but its ideal (isentropic) outlet state would be wet.
- **Why:** This version computes a turbine's ideal outlet in the phase declared for the real outlet. Here the ideal outlet entropy &lt;s_star&gt; is below the saturated-vapour entropy &lt;s_saturated&gt; at &lt;pressure&gt;, so the ideal state is two-phase. This is a limitation of the software (L-TH-4), not an error in your flowsheet.
- **Do:** Re-declare the outlet &lt;outlet&gt; as wet ("vapor_liquid") if it can be wet at your conditions. If that is refused as a phase mismatch, change the operating conditions (for example the turbine inlet temperature or outlet pressure) until the ideal and the real outlet are in the same phase. Support for this case is planned (the std.turbine model).
- **Parameters:** `unit` (unit), `outlet` (stream, optional), `phase` (enum, optional), `s_star` (quantity, optional), `s_saturated` (quantity, optional), `pressure` (quantity, optional)
- **Not supported:** limitation [`L-TH-4`](limitations.md#L-TH-4) (its row in the [support matrix](https://github.com/computational-chemical-engineering/openflowsheet/blob/main/docs/support-matrix.md)); missing capability: a vapour turbine outlet with a two-phase isentropic reference
- **See also:** [`phase_regime_mismatch`](#phase_regime_mismatch), [`L-TH-4`](limitations.md#L-TH-4)

Example:

```text
The solve stopped before its first iteration: unit 'T' could not compute its outlets from the starting values.
  Cause:   Unit 'T' needs a case this version does not support: its outlet 'S4' is declared vapour, but its ideal (isentropic) outlet state would be wet.
  Why:     This version computes a turbine's ideal outlet in the phase declared for the real outlet. Here the ideal outlet entropy 140.2 J/(mol*K) is below the saturated-vapour entropy 146.3 J/(mol*K) at 10000 Pa, so the ideal state is two-phase. This is a limitation of the software (L-TH-4), not an error in your flowsheet.
  Do:      Re-declare the outlet 'S4' as wet ("vapor_liquid") if it can be wet at your conditions. If that is refused as a phase mismatch, change the operating conditions (for example the turbine inlet temperature or outlet pressure) until the ideal and the real outlet are in the same phase. Support for this case is planned (the std.turbine model).
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    isentropic_state_two_phase, in INITIALIZATION_FAILED → initializer_failed (openflowsheet explain isentropic_state_two_phase)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#isentropic_state_two_phase
```

<a id="model_unsupported"></a>

## `model_unsupported`: No model with this id is available

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** No model with the id "&lt;model&gt;" is available in this version.
- **Why:** Each unit names the model that computes it. This version computes only the models it lists, and a unit's model id must match one of them exactly, prefix included (for example thermal.heater).
- **Do:** Compare the unit's model id with the available models (the list_models operation, or openflowsheet api list_models): correct its spelling, or choose a listed model that does what the unit needs.
- **Parameters:** `model` (text)
- **Not supported:** missing capability: a unit model with this id
- **See also:** [`revision_not_ready`](api-errors.md#revision_not_ready)

Example:

```text
No model with the id "thermal.boiler" is available in this version.
  Why:     Each unit names the model that computes it. This version computes only the models it lists, and a unit's model id must match one of them exactly, prefix included (for example thermal.heater).
  Do:      Compare the unit's model id with the available models (the list_models operation, or openflowsheet api list_models): correct its spelling, or choose a listed model that does what the unit needs.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    model_unsupported (openflowsheet explain model_unsupported)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#model_unsupported
```

<a id="namespace_conflict"></a>

## `namespace_conflict`: Two installed extensions use the same namespace

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** Two installed distributions declare the namespace &lt;namespace&gt;, so neither is loaded.
- **Why:** A namespace identifies one extension. When two different distributions declare it, the registry cannot tell which one an id belongs to, so it loads neither. One distribution found twice on the import path is not a conflict.
- **Do:** Uninstall one of the two distributions, or give one of them another namespace.
- **Parameters:** `namespace` (text)
- **See also:** [`reserved_namespace`](#reserved_namespace)

Example:

```text
Two installed distributions declare the namespace acme, so neither is loaded.
  Why:     A namespace identifies one extension. When two different distributions declare it, the registry cannot tell which one an id belongs to, so it loads neither. One distribution found twice on the import path is not a conflict.
  Do:      Uninstall one of the two distributions, or give one of them another namespace.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    namespace_conflict (openflowsheet explain namespace_conflict)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#namespace_conflict
```

<a id="nlp_solver_unavailable"></a>

## `nlp_solver_unavailable`: Optimisation without the audited NLP solver

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** This installation cannot optimise: the audited NLP solver is not available here.
- **Why:** Optimisation solves with Ipopt, reached through Pyomo and cyipopt, in the versions whose licences and binaries were audited: the nlp extra's audited environment on Linux x86-64. Without it this version refuses to optimise rather than run an unaudited solver.
- **Do:** To optimise, use the audited nlp environment on Linux x86-64 (user guide, section "The nlp extra"); to check the revision for a solve, validate it with the task "simulation".
- **Not supported:** limitation [`L-OPT-1`](limitations.md#L-OPT-1) (its row in the [support matrix](https://github.com/computational-chemical-engineering/openflowsheet/blob/main/docs/support-matrix.md)); missing capability: optimisation outside the audited nlp environment on Linux x86-64
- **See also:** [`unsupported`](api-errors.md#unsupported)

Example:

```text
This installation cannot optimise: the audited NLP solver is not available here.
  Why:     Optimisation solves with Ipopt, reached through Pyomo and cyipopt, in the versions whose licences and binaries were audited: the nlp extra's audited environment on Linux x86-64. Without it this version refuses to optimise rather than run an unaudited solver.
  Do:      To optimise, use the audited nlp environment on Linux x86-64 (user guide, section "The nlp extra"); to check the revision for a solve, validate it with the task "simulation".
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    nlp_solver_unavailable, in unsupported (openflowsheet explain nlp_solver_unavailable)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#nlp_solver_unavailable
```

<a id="not_a_directory"></a>

## `not_a_directory`: The path is a file, not a directory

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** &lt;directory&gt; is a file, not a directory; a project needs a new or empty directory.
- **Why:** A project is a directory that holds its database and its files, so it cannot be made at the path of an existing file.
- **Do:** Choose another path for the project, or move or rename the file.
- **Parameters:** `directory` (directory)
- **See also:** [`project_exists`](#project_exists), [`directory_not_empty`](#directory_not_empty)

Example:

```text
'plant.txt' is a file, not a directory; a project needs a new or empty directory.
  Why:     A project is a directory that holds its database and its files, so it cannot be made at the path of an existing file.
  Do:      Choose another path for the project, or move or rename the file.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    not_a_directory (openflowsheet explain not_a_directory)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#not_a_directory
```

<a id="not_a_project"></a>

## `not_a_project`: The directory does not hold a project

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** Directory &lt;directory&gt; is not a project: it holds no project database.
- **Why:** Opening a project reads the database (project.sqlite3) that creating the project wrote into its directory. This directory has none: it was never made a project, or it is not the directory you meant.
- **Do:** Check the path: give the directory the project was created in, or create a new project here.
- **Parameters:** `directory` (directory)
- **See also:** [`project_exists`](#project_exists)

Example:

```text
Directory 'plant' is not a project: it holds no project database.
  Why:     Opening a project reads the database (project.sqlite3) that creating the project wrote into its directory. This directory has none: it was never made a project, or it is not the directory you meant.
  Do:      Check the path: give the directory the project was created in, or create a new project here.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    not_a_project (openflowsheet explain not_a_project)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#not_a_project
```

<a id="out_of_domain"></a>

## `out_of_domain`: A state outside the range of the property method

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** A property calculation for unit &lt;unit&gt; was asked for a state outside the range its property method covers.
- **Why:** A property method is valid only over a stated range of temperature and pressure, and outside it OpenFlowsheet stops instead of extrapolating. The method reported: &lt;detail&gt;. For example, water's IAPWS-95 method in this version covers 273.16 K to 1273.15 K and 100 Pa to 100 MPa.
- **Do:** Check the temperatures and pressures specified for the streams that reach &lt;unit&gt;, for example a feed below the freezing point, and bring them inside the property method's range; the limitations page lists the range of each method.
- **Parameters:** `unit` (unit, optional), `detail` (text, optional), `what` (text, optional), `value` (quantity, optional), `low` (quantity, optional), `high` (quantity, optional)
- **See also:** [`initializer_failed`](#initializer_failed)

Example:

```text
The solve stopped before its first iteration: unit 'P' could not compute its outlets from the starting values.
  Cause:   A property calculation for unit 'P' was asked for a state outside the range its property method covers.
  Why:     A property method is valid only over a stated range of temperature and pressure, and outside it OpenFlowsheet stops instead of extrapolating. Here the temperature 200.0 K is outside the method's range of 273.2 K to 1273 K.
  Do:      Check the temperatures and pressures specified for the streams that reach 'P', for example a feed below the freezing point, and bring them inside the property method's range; the limitations page lists the range of each method.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    out_of_domain, in INITIALIZATION_FAILED → initializer_failed (openflowsheet explain out_of_domain)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#out_of_domain
```

Example:

```text
The solve stopped: no step along its search direction reduced the error.
  Cause:   A property calculation for unit 'B' was asked for a state outside the range its property method covers.
  Why:     A property method is valid only over a stated range of temperature and pressure, and outside it OpenFlowsheet stops instead of extrapolating. For example, water's IAPWS-95 method in this version covers 273.16 K to 1273.15 K and 100 Pa to 100 MPa.
  Do:      The solver reached a state outside the property method's range at unit 'B' while iterating; the specified states may all be inside it. Give initial guesses closer to the expected solution, or check the specifications that drive the solve towards that state; the limitations page lists the range of each method.
  Kind:    Numerical failure: the solver did not find the solution; your flowsheet may be correct.
  Code:    out_of_domain, in LINE_SEARCH_FAILED (openflowsheet explain out_of_domain)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#out_of_domain
```

<a id="phase_regime_mismatch"></a>

## `phase_regime_mismatch`: Declared phase does not match the computed state

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** Stream &lt;stream&gt; is not in its declared phase: it is declared &lt;declared&gt;, but at these conditions it is &lt;landed&gt;.
- **Where:** stream &lt;stream&gt;, an outlet of unit &lt;unit&gt; (&lt;unit_model&gt;)
- **Why:** Each stream carries a declared phase, and a unit computes its outlet only in that phase.
- **Do:** Change the phase declared for &lt;stream&gt; to the one that matches the computed state.
- **Parameters:** `stream` (stream), `unit` (unit, optional), `declared` (enum, optional), `landed` (enum, optional), `vapour_fraction` (number, optional), `property` (enum, optional), `value` (quantity, optional), `saturated_liquid` (quantity, optional), `saturated_vapour` (quantity, optional), `pressure` (quantity, optional)
- **See also:** [`isentropic_state_two_phase`](#isentropic_state_two_phase), [`L-TH-3`](limitations.md#L-TH-3)

Example:

```text
The solve stopped before its first iteration: unit 'T' could not compute its outlets from the starting values.
  Cause:   Stream 'S4' is not in its declared phase: it is declared wet (vapour + liquid), but at these conditions it is vapour.
  Why:     At 10000 Pa the enthalpy of 'S4' is 47330 J/mol, above the saturated-vapour value 46570 J/mol, so the stream is vapour, not wet (vapour + liquid).
  Do:      Declare 'S4' as vapour. If you expected wet (vapour + liquid), check the specifications that set the conditions upstream of 'S4'.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    phase_regime_mismatch, in INITIALIZATION_FAILED → initializer_failed (openflowsheet explain phase_regime_mismatch)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#phase_regime_mismatch
```

<a id="platform_unsupported"></a>

## `platform_unsupported`: An extension does not run on this platform

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** The extension &lt;id&gt; does not run on &lt;platform&gt;.
- **Why:** An extension's descriptor lists the platforms its implementation runs on. Admission does not depend on the platform, but constructing the extension does, and this platform is not on its list.
- **Do:** Run on one of the platforms the extension lists, or choose another extension that provides the same capabilities.
- **Parameters:** `id` (text), `platform` (text)
- **Not supported:** missing capability: this extension on this platform
- **See also:** [`dependency_missing`](#dependency_missing)

Example:

```text
The extension acme.slurry-mixer does not run on linux-aarch64.
  Why:     An extension's descriptor lists the platforms its implementation runs on. Admission does not depend on the platform, but constructing the extension does, and this platform is not on its list.
  Do:      Run on one of the platforms the extension lists, or choose another extension that provides the same capabilities.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    platform_unsupported (openflowsheet explain platform_unsupported)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#platform_unsupported
```

<a id="pressure_fall"></a>

## `pressure_fall`: An outlet pressure below the inlet pressure of a machine that can only raise it

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The outlet pressure specified for unit &lt;unit&gt;, a &lt;machine&gt;, is below its inlet pressure (&lt;p_spec&gt; against &lt;p_inlet&gt;).
- **Why:** A pump or a compressor does work on the fluid to raise its pressure, so its outlet pressure cannot be below its inlet pressure. Lowering the pressure takes a valve or a turbine.
- **Do:** Give the &lt;machine&gt; &lt;unit&gt; an outlet pressure at or above its inlet pressure of &lt;p_inlet&gt;, or lower the pressure upstream of it.
- **Parameters:** `machine` (text), `p_spec` (quantity, optional), `p_inlet` (quantity, optional), `unit` (unit, optional)
- **See also:** [`pressure_rise`](#pressure_rise)

Example:

```text
The solve stopped before its first iteration: unit 'P' could not compute its outlets from the starting values.
  Cause:   The outlet pressure specified for unit 'P', a pump, is below its inlet pressure (50000 Pa against 100000 Pa).
  Why:     A pump or a compressor does work on the fluid to raise its pressure, so its outlet pressure cannot be below its inlet pressure. Lowering the pressure takes a valve or a turbine.
  Do:      Give the pump 'P' an outlet pressure at or above its inlet pressure of 100000 Pa, or lower the pressure upstream of it.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    pressure_fall, in INITIALIZATION_FAILED → initializer_failed (openflowsheet explain pressure_fall)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#pressure_fall
```

<a id="pressure_rise"></a>

## `pressure_rise`: An outlet pressure above the inlet pressure of a unit that can only lower it

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The outlet pressure specified for unit &lt;unit&gt;, a &lt;machine&gt;, is above its inlet pressure (&lt;p_spec&gt; against &lt;p_inlet&gt;).
- **Why:** A turbine expands the fluid that passes through it, so it can only lower the pressure. Raising the pressure takes a pump or a compressor.
- **Do:** Give the &lt;machine&gt; &lt;unit&gt; an outlet pressure at or below its inlet pressure of &lt;p_inlet&gt;, or raise the pressure upstream of it (for example a pump's outlet pressure).
- **Parameters:** `machine` (text), `unit` (unit, optional), `p_spec` (quantity, optional), `p_inlet` (quantity, optional)

Example:

```text
The solve stopped before its first iteration: unit 'T' could not compute its outlets from the starting values.
  Cause:   The outlet pressure specified for unit 'T', a turbine, is above its inlet pressure (5000000 Pa against 3000000 Pa).
  Why:     A turbine expands the fluid that passes through it, so it can only lower the pressure. Raising the pressure takes a pump or a compressor.
  Do:      Give the turbine 'T' an outlet pressure at or below its inlet pressure of 3000000 Pa, or raise the pressure upstream of it (for example a pump's outlet pressure).
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    pressure_rise, in INITIALIZATION_FAILED → initializer_failed (openflowsheet explain pressure_rise)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#pressure_rise
```

Example:

```text
The solve stopped before its first iteration: unit 'V' could not compute its outlets from the starting values.
  Cause:   The outlet pressure specified for unit 'V', a valve, is above its inlet pressure (200000 Pa against 100000 Pa).
  Why:     A valve throttles the fluid that passes through it, so it can only lower the pressure. Raising the pressure takes a pump or a compressor.
  Do:      Give the valve 'V' an outlet pressure at or below its inlet pressure of 100000 Pa, or raise the pressure upstream of it (for example a pump's outlet pressure).
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    pressure_rise, in INITIALIZATION_FAILED → initializer_failed (openflowsheet explain pressure_rise)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#pressure_rise
```

<a id="project_exists"></a>

## `project_exists`: The directory already holds a project

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** Directory &lt;directory&gt; is not empty: it already holds a project, and create() needs a new or empty directory.
- **Why:** create() makes a new project and never reuses a directory, so a re-run cannot overwrite work silently.
- **Do:** To use the existing project, open it instead.
- **Parameters:** `directory` (directory)

Example:

```text
Directory 'plant' is not empty: it already holds a project, and create() needs a new or empty directory.
  Why:     create() makes a new project and never reuses a directory, so a re-run cannot overwrite work silently.
  Do:      To use the existing project, open it instead.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    project_exists (openflowsheet explain project_exists)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#project_exists
```

<a id="project_id_mismatch"></a>

## `project_id_mismatch`: The directory holds a project with another id

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** Directory &lt;directory&gt; holds the project '&lt;existing&gt;', not '&lt;project_id&gt;'.
- **Why:** Asked to reuse an existing project, OpenFlowsheet opens it only when its id is the one requested, so a script never works on another project by mistake.
- **Do:** To open the project that is there, ask for its id '&lt;existing&gt;' or give no id; to create '&lt;project_id&gt;', choose another directory.
- **Parameters:** `directory` (directory), `project_id` (text), `existing` (text)
- **See also:** [`project_exists`](#project_exists)

Example:

```text
Directory 'plant' holds the project 'plant-a', not 'plant-b'.
  Why:     Asked to reuse an existing project, OpenFlowsheet opens it only when its id is the one requested, so a script never works on another project by mistake.
  Do:      To open the project that is there, ask for its id 'plant-a' or give no id; to create 'plant-b', choose another directory.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    project_id_mismatch (openflowsheet explain project_id_mismatch)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#project_id_mismatch
```

<a id="property_evaluation_failed"></a>

## `property_evaluation_failed`: A property of one phase of a stream could not be evaluated

**Kind:** Numerical failure: the solver did not find the solution; your flowsheet may be correct.

- **Summary:** The property &lt;property&gt; of the &lt;phase&gt; phase of stream &lt;stream&gt; could not be evaluated (status &lt;status&gt;).
- **Where:** stream &lt;stream&gt;
- **Why:** The property basis was asked for &lt;property&gt; at the temperature, pressure and composition of this phase and returned no value. The quantities that need it are left empty.
- **Do:** Check that the temperature and pressure of &lt;stream&gt; lie in the range the property basis covers; the other values of &lt;stream&gt; are unaffected.
- **Parameters:** `stream` (stream), `phase` (text), `property` (text), `status` (text, optional)
- **See also:** [`stream_enthalpy_absent`](notices.md#stream_enthalpy_absent)

Example:

```text
The property h of the LIQUID phase of stream 'S4' could not be evaluated (status out_of_range).
  Why:     The property basis was asked for h at the temperature, pressure and composition of this phase and returned no value. The quantities that need it are left empty.
  Do:      Check that the temperature and pressure of 'S4' lie in the range the property basis covers; the other values of 'S4' are unaffected.
  Kind:    Numerical failure: the solver did not find the solution; your flowsheet may be correct.
  Code:    property_evaluation_failed (openflowsheet explain property_evaluation_failed)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#property_evaluation_failed
```

<a id="property_not_provided"></a>

## `property_not_provided`: The property basis does not provide this property

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** The property basis &lt;provider&gt; does not provide the property &lt;property&gt;, so the values that need it are not given.
- **Why:** The stream table reports only what the flowsheet's property basis computes. It does not put an estimate (an ideal-gas density, for example) in place of a property the basis does not offer.
- **Do:** Use a property basis that provides &lt;property&gt; if you need these values; the other values of the table are unaffected.
- **Parameters:** `provider` (text), `property` (text)
- **Not supported:** missing capability: this property from the flowsheet's property basis
- **See also:** [`stream_enthalpy_absent`](notices.md#stream_enthalpy_absent)

Example:

```text
The property basis wilson-ig-v2 does not provide the property v, so the values that need it are not given.
  Why:     The stream table reports only what the flowsheet's property basis computes. It does not put an estimate (an ideal-gas density, for example) in place of a property the basis does not offer.
  Do:      Use a property basis that provides v if you need these values; the other values of the table are unaffected.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    property_not_provided (openflowsheet explain property_not_provided)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#property_not_provided
```

<a id="registry_closed"></a>

## `registry_closed`: Something tried to register an extension after the registry was built

**Kind:** Internal error in OpenFlowsheet: please report it.

- **Summary:** An extension was registered after the registry was built and closed.
- **Why:** The registry is built once, at start, from the built-in tables and the installed entry points, and then closed so that what is loaded cannot change during a session. Registering afterwards is a programming error.
- **Do:** Report this as a bug, with the steps that led to it.

Example:

```text
An extension was registered after the registry was built and closed.
  Why:     The registry is built once, at start, from the built-in tables and the installed entry points, and then closed so that what is loaded cannot change during a session. Registering afterwards is a programming error.
  Do:      Report this as a bug, with the steps that led to it.
  Kind:    Internal error in OpenFlowsheet: please report it.
  Code:    registry_closed (openflowsheet explain registry_closed)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#registry_closed
```

<a id="request_invalid"></a>

## `request_invalid`: An optimisation request that breaks its schema or rules

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The optimisation request is invalid.
- **Why:** Before anything is solved, an optimisation request (its decisions and their bounds, the objective, the constraints and the starts) is checked against its schema and the rules stated for its members, and this one breaks one of them. The check reported: &lt;detail&gt;.
- **Do:** Correct the request as the check reports, and send it again.
- **Parameters:** `member` (pointer), `detail` (text, optional)

Example:

```text
The optimisation request is invalid at /decisions/0/upper.
  Why:     Before anything is solved, an optimisation request (its decisions and their bounds, the objective, the constraints and the starts) is checked against its schema and the rules stated for its members, and this one breaks one of them. The check reported: 'high' is not of type 'number'.
  Do:      Correct the member at /decisions/0/upper as the check reports, and send the request again.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    request_invalid, in invalid_request (openflowsheet explain request_invalid)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#request_invalid
```

Example:

```text
The optimisation request is invalid.
  Why:     Before anything is solved, an optimisation request (its decisions and their bounds, the objective, the constraints and the starts) is checked against its schema and the rules stated for its members, and this one breaks one of them. The check reported: 'decisions' is a required property.
  Do:      Correct the request as the check reports, and send it again.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    request_invalid, in invalid_request (openflowsheet explain request_invalid)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#request_invalid
```

<a id="reserved_capability"></a>

## `reserved_capability`: An extension names a capability reserved for others

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The capability &lt;token&gt; is reserved, so the extension that declares it is not loaded.
- **Why:** Capabilities in the legacy space describe the property methods built into OpenFlowsheet; no extension may require or provide them, because the built-in unit models cannot run on an extension's method. A capability in the x space may be provided only by an extension of the namespace it names.
- **Do:** Remove the capability from the extension's descriptor, or, for an x capability, provide it from the extension whose namespace it names.
- **Parameters:** `token` (text)
- **See also:** [`capability_unknown`](#capability_unknown)

Example:

```text
The capability legacy:syn001 is reserved, so the extension that declares it is not loaded.
  Why:     Capabilities in the legacy space describe the property methods built into OpenFlowsheet; no extension may require or provide them, because the built-in unit models cannot run on an extension's method. A capability in the x space may be provided only by an extension of the namespace it names.
  Do:      Remove the capability from the extension's descriptor, or, for an x capability, provide it from the extension whose namespace it names.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    reserved_capability (openflowsheet explain reserved_capability)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#reserved_capability
```

<a id="reserved_namespace"></a>

## `reserved_namespace`: An extension uses a reserved namespace

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The namespace &lt;namespace&gt; is reserved, so the extension package that uses it is not loaded.
- **Why:** An extension's namespace is the name of its entry point, and every id it registers starts with it. The first segment of every built-in id, and openflowsheet, core, std, legacy, x and user, are reserved so that an extension can never take a built-in's id.
- **Do:** Rename the extension's entry point to a namespace of its own, and start every id the package declares with it.
- **Parameters:** `namespace` (text)
- **See also:** [`namespace_conflict`](#namespace_conflict)

Example:

```text
The namespace thermal is reserved, so the extension package that uses it is not loaded.
  Why:     An extension's namespace is the name of its entry point, and every id it registers starts with it. The first segment of every built-in id, and openflowsheet, core, std, legacy, x and user, are reserved so that an extension can never take a built-in's id.
  Do:      Rename the extension's entry point to a namespace of its own, and start every id the package declares with it.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    reserved_namespace (openflowsheet explain reserved_namespace)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#reserved_namespace
```

<a id="self_hash_unavailable"></a>

## `self_hash_unavailable`: A file of an extension's implementation cannot be read

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The file &lt;path&gt; of extension &lt;id&gt; cannot be read, so its package is not loaded.
- **Why:** The registry identifies each extension by a hash of the files its descriptor lists, read from the directory its top-level package is installed in. This file is not a regular file there. Extensions installed as a zip file or as a namespace package have no such directory and cannot be hashed.
- **Do:** Install the extension as an ordinary package directory, and list in its descriptor only files the package contains.
- **Parameters:** `id` (text), `path` (text)

Example:

```text
The file acme/units/mixer.py of extension acme.slurry-mixer cannot be read, so its package is not loaded.
  Why:     The registry identifies each extension by a hash of the files its descriptor lists, read from the directory its top-level package is installed in. This file is not a regular file there. Extensions installed as a zip file or as a namespace package have no such directory and cannot be hashed.
  Do:      Install the extension as an ordinary package directory, and list in its descriptor only files the package contains.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    self_hash_unavailable (openflowsheet explain self_hash_unavailable)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#self_hash_unavailable
```

<a id="specification_missing"></a>

## `specification_missing`: A value that no specification fixes

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The revision is incomplete: no specification fixes &lt;column&gt; (on &lt;object&gt;).
- **Why:** A solve needs every value its units leave free to be fixed by exactly one specification. Here &lt;column&gt; is left free, so the equations do not determine the state.
- **Do:** Add one fixed specification for &lt;column&gt;, for example with target &lt;object&gt;; the check's message lists the kind, unit and target each choice takes.
- **Parameters:** `column` (text), `object` (element, optional)
- **See also:** [`specification_unconsumed`](#specification_unconsumed), [`revision_not_ready`](api-errors.md#revision_not_ready)

Example:

```text
The revision is incomplete: no specification fixes S4.P (on 'S4').
  Why:     A solve needs every value its units leave free to be fixed by exactly one specification. Here S4.P is left free, so the equations do not determine the state.
  Do:      Add one fixed specification for S4.P, for example with target 'S4'; the check's message lists the kind, unit and target each choice takes.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    specification_missing, in revision_not_ready (openflowsheet explain specification_missing)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#specification_missing
```

<a id="specification_unconsumed"></a>

## `specification_unconsumed`: A specification that no unit reads

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** Specification &lt;specification&gt; sets a value that no unit reads: unit &lt;unit&gt; (&lt;model&gt;) does not read &lt;column&gt;.
- **Why:** Each specification must fix a value a unit's model reads. One that nothing reads would be ignored silently, so validation refuses it; it usually means one specification too many, or one on the wrong variable or object.
- **Do:** Remove &lt;specification&gt;, or change its target to a value the unit reads (&lt;unit&gt; reads &lt;reads&gt;, among others); the check's message lists the kind, unit and target each one takes.
- **Parameters:** `specification` (specification), `unit` (unit, optional), `model` (text, optional), `column` (text, optional), `reads` (text, optional)
- **See also:** [`specification_missing`](#specification_missing), [`revision_not_ready`](api-errors.md#revision_not_ready)

Example:

```text
Specification 'pump-T' sets a value that no unit reads: unit 'P' (thermal.pump) does not read S2.T.
  Why:     Each specification must fix a value a unit's model reads. One that nothing reads would be ignored silently, so validation refuses it; it usually means one specification too many, or one on the wrong variable or object.
  Do:      Remove 'pump-T', or change its target to a value the unit reads ('P' reads outlet_pressure, among others); the check's message lists the kind, unit and target each one takes.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    specification_unconsumed, in revision_not_ready (openflowsheet explain specification_unconsumed)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#specification_unconsumed
```

<a id="specification_unit_unsupported"></a>

## `specification_unit_unsupported`: A specification's unit that its quantity kind does not take

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** Specification &lt;specification&gt; gives its value in a unit its quantity kind does not take: a &lt;quantity&gt; takes &lt;units&gt;.
- **Why:** Validation accepts for each quantity kind only the units listed for it, spelled exactly: unit symbols are case-sensitive, so a temperature takes "degC" but not "degc".
- **Do:** Correct the spelling of the unit of &lt;specification&gt; to one of &lt;units&gt;, or give the value in one of the accepted units.
- **Parameters:** `specification` (specification), `quantity` (text, optional), `units` (text, optional)
- **See also:** [`DIM-01`](checks.md#DIM-01), [`revision_not_ready`](api-errors.md#revision_not_ready)

Example:

```text
Specification 'boiler-T' gives its value in a unit its quantity kind does not take: a temperature takes K, degC, degF.
  Why:     Validation accepts for each quantity kind only the units listed for it, spelled exactly: unit symbols are case-sensitive, so a temperature takes "degC" but not "degc".
  Do:      Correct the spelling of the unit of 'boiler-T' to one of K, degC, degF, or give the value in one of the accepted units.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    specification_unit_unsupported, in revision_not_ready → DIM-01 (openflowsheet explain specification_unit_unsupported)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#specification_unit_unsupported
```

<a id="task_unsupported"></a>

## `task_unsupported`: A change checked for a task other than simulation

**Kind:** Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.

- **Summary:** A change is checked for the task "simulation" only; this version cannot check it for the "&lt;task&gt;" task.
- **Why:** Committing or previewing a change validates the new revision for the change's task. Validating for optimization needs an optimization request (decisions, objective and starts), and a change carries none, so this version refuses rather than report a revision ready for a task it has not checked.
- **Do:** Commit the change with the task "simulation"; then validate the committed revision with the task "optimization" and an optimization request.
- **Parameters:** `task` (text)
- **Not supported:** missing capability: checking a change for the optimization task when it is committed or previewed
- **See also:** [`unsupported`](api-errors.md#unsupported)

Example:

```text
A change is checked for the task "simulation" only; this version cannot check it for the "optimization" task.
  Why:     Committing or previewing a change validates the new revision for the change's task. Validating for optimization needs an optimization request (decisions, objective and starts), and a change carries none, so this version refuses rather than report a revision ready for a task it has not checked.
  Do:      Commit the change with the task "simulation"; then validate the committed revision with the task "optimization" and an optimization request.
  Kind:    Not supported in this version: a limitation of OpenFlowsheet, not an error in your flowsheet.
  Code:    task_unsupported, in unsupported (openflowsheet explain task_unsupported)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#task_unsupported
```

<a id="value_not_finite"></a>

## `value_not_finite`: A computed value is not a finite number

**Kind:** Numerical failure: the solver did not find the solution; your flowsheet may be correct.

- **Summary:** The value &lt;quantity&gt; of &lt;subject&gt; is not a finite number, so it is not given.
- **Why:** A computed value overflowed, or a quotient had no defined value; the table gives no value rather than an infinite or undefined one.
- **Do:** Check the flows and conditions of &lt;subject&gt;: a very large or very small flow can put a value outside the range of floating-point numbers.
- **Parameters:** `subject` (text), `quantity` (text)
- **See also:** [`stream_enthalpy_absent`](notices.md#stream_enthalpy_absent)

Example:

```text
The value H_flow of S6 is not a finite number, so it is not given.
  Why:     A computed value overflowed, or a quotient had no defined value; the table gives no value rather than an infinite or undefined one.
  Do:      Check the flows and conditions of S6: a very large or very small flow can put a value outside the range of floating-point numbers.
  Kind:    Numerical failure: the solver did not find the solution; your flowsheet may be correct.
  Code:    value_not_finite (openflowsheet explain value_not_finite)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#value_not_finite
```

<a id="warm_start_source_missing"></a>

## `warm_start_source_missing`: A warm start from a job with no solution state

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The declared warm start names job &lt;job_id&gt;, which is not a solve job of this project with a solution state.
- **Why:** A warm start declared by job id starts the solve from that job's solution state, so the job must be a solve job of this project that wrote one. Its certificate status does not matter.
- **Do:** Name a solve job of this project whose run wrote a solution state, or leave the job id out of the warm start.
- **Parameters:** `job_id` (job)

Example:

```text
The declared warm start names job 'job-000003', which is not a solve job of this project with a solution state.
  Why:     A warm start declared by job id starts the solve from that job's solution state, so the job must be a solve job of this project that wrote one. Its certificate status does not matter.
  Do:      Name a solve job of this project whose run wrote a solution state, or leave the job id out of the warm start.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    warm_start_source_missing, in invalid_request (openflowsheet explain warm_start_source_missing)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#warm_start_source_missing
```

<a id="warm_start_unit_unknown"></a>

## `warm_start_unit_unknown`: A coupling start for a unit the revision does not have

**Kind:** Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.

- **Summary:** The declared warm start gives a coupling start for '&lt;unit&gt;', which is not a unit of this revision.
- **Why:** A warm start may give, for each unit computed by an external program, starting values for what the flowsheet and that program exchange (the coupling), keyed by the unit's instance id; so each key must be a unit of the revision being solved. Whether the unit is computed by an external program in this solve is checked when the run starts; a start that fails that check is recorded as rejected, not refused.
- **Do:** Key each coupling start by the instance id of a unit in this revision, or remove the key '&lt;unit&gt;'.
- **Parameters:** `unit` (text)

Example:

```text
The declared warm start gives a coupling start for 'R9', which is not a unit of this revision.
  Why:     A warm start may give, for each unit computed by an external program, starting values for what the flowsheet and that program exchange (the coupling), keyed by the unit's instance id; so each key must be a unit of the revision being solved. Whether the unit is computed by an external program in this solve is checked when the run starts; a start that fails that check is recorded as rejected, not refused.
  Do:      Key each coupling start by the instance id of a unit in this revision, or remove the key 'R9'.
  Kind:    Input problem: something in the flowsheet or the request needs to change.
  Code:    warm_start_unit_unknown, in invalid_request (openflowsheet explain warm_start_unit_unknown)
  Docs:    https://computational-chemical-engineering.github.io/openflowsheet/messages/refusals/#warm_start_unit_unknown
```
